title: Mirror route + module-view joint factorization
hypothesis: Route IDs plus one phase per stage reproduce aligned tasks using less serialized state than direct coefficients; unrelated tasks expose private fallback cost.
physical_object: four 2x2 modules at each of two stages
mirror_coordinate: per-task route IDs x one Givens phase per stage; exact private fallback for unrelated tasks
logical_multiplicity: 32 functions from an 8-module bank plus two stage codes or private matrices
controls: direct sine/cosine coefficients for each route-stage view
fixture: 24 aligned tasks use route-selected matrices conjugated by task-specific phases; 8 unrelated tasks use independent matrices. Input/output dimension 2 with ReLU between linear stages.

development.selection_metric: normalized task-output MSE, actual serialized bytes, decode+forward MAC proxy, CPU latency

fresh.run_only_if: do not run: development payload and Mirror-attribution gates failed

compute.timing_boundary: decode routes/views, materialize matrices, and run 256 queries

success_gate: All fresh aligned tasks nMSE<=1e-6; Mirror payload<=0.90x direct coefficient payload and <=0.75x independent payload; Mirror MAC proxy<=1.5x direct coefficients.
failure_gate: Any quality or payload gate miss, or exact native-control function/byte alias.
boundaries: Synthetic analytic task family, no training or learned router.
Oracle task IDs are charged as route-table bytes; no routing-quality claim.
Task count is not independent-capacity evidence.
